title: Absolute trust that pardon is already obtained is not the essential formal act of justifying faith
source_text: XXI. Porro cum fides vera, licet infirma, saltem ad tempus consistere possit absque fiducia certa & absoluta de obtenta a Deo remissione peccatorum, & nostra per Christi gratiam reconciliatione, inde patet fiduciam istam non esse essentialem & formalem actum fidei salvificae atque justificantis. Nec enim fides justificans unquam consistere potest sine actu suo proprio & formali.
pass_a_gloss: Further, since true faith, though weak, can at least for a time stand without a certain and absolute confidence concerning remission of sins already obtained from God and our reconciliation through Christ’s grace, it is plain that that confidence is not the essential and formal act of saving and justifying faith. For justifying faith can never stand without its proper and formal act.
pass_b_english: Weak true faith can temporarily lack absolute assurance of already-obtained pardon.
Therefore that assurance is not faith’s essential formal act.
